segments.t: Max finds Barinov in a dark mood and asks what's wrong. The chef has lost money on football, but that's not the worst of it. He has a piece of news for Max, and it's about Vika. Listen to the tone before the words.

Макс, не задавай мне глупых вопросов.
Вы опять проиграли деньги на ставках?
Я бы сейчас с удовольствием выпил водки.
Что ещё неприятного у вас случилось?
Дело вовсе не в моих ставках.
А в чём тогда настоящая проблема?
У меня есть для тебя важная новость.
Тётя Вика сказала, что любит тебя.
Что? Этого просто не может быть!
Она сама призналась мне в этом.
Шеф, вы точно не шутите сейчас?
Здравствуйте, шеф, как ваши дела сегодня?

'Hello, chef, how are your affairs today?' Russians ask the words for "how are your affairs", in the multiple, where we say "how are you". With a friend it's just the words for "how affairs". Max has no idea what he's in for.

'Did you lose money on bets again?' When they say 'did you lose' is the losing-in-a-game word the mother used in the first scene. When they say 'on bets' takes the location ending after the connecting word. Max has guessed, and he's right.
Я бы сейчас с удовольствием выпил водки.

'I would gladly drink vodka right now.' A short little word makes "would", and it goes with the past: "I would drank". Notice the part 'with pleasure' is Russian for "gladly". Notice the part 'vodka' takes the "of" ending to mean "some vodka".
Что ещё неприятного у вас случилось?

'What else unpleasant has happened to you?' In Russian, 'unpleasant' translates reads "not pleasant", keeping the "of" ending after the words for "what else". In Russian, 'has happened to you' translates translates literally as "at you happened". Max uses the polite In Russian, 'you' translates.

'The matter is not at all about my bets.' Russians say "the matter is in", and then the thing. So the sentence is literally "the matter is not in my bets". Here, 'at all' shows is used here for emphasis.

'Then what is the real problem?' The way to express 'and in what' picks up the "in" connecting word from the chef's line. The way to express 'real' is the word from in "true friend". The way to express 'problem' sounds just like English.

'I have important news for you.' Here Russian does add 'there is' is used here: literally "at me there is for you". It stresses that he has something. Barinov uses the casual 'you' is used here.

'What news, chef, tell me quickly.' Listen to how 'what' carries the she-word ending as Listen to how 'news' is a she-word. The action Listen to how 'speak' takes the polite multiple ending. Listen to how 'quickly' takes the comparative ending for "quicker".
Тётя Вика сказала, что любит тебя.
'Aunt Vika said that she loves you.' Barinov keeps his daughter's way of saying it, the words for "aunt Vika". There's no "she" in the Russian, only the words for "said that loves you".

'What? That simply cannot be!' After They express 'not' by, They express 'that' by takes the "of" ending: "that cannot be" is a set phrase. And the words for "can be" on their own mean "maybe".

'She herself confessed this to me.' We hear 'herself' gives the claim weight. We hear 'confessed' takes the self-directed ending for a woman. We hear 'in this' is used because Russians confess "in" something.

Max can't quite believe it, and he asks whether it's a joke. The news came from a little girl, and it will turn his day upside down. Until next time.
